::: page-header
# Teaching
:::

I teach psychology as a practical discipline: concepts first, then the tools that let students test and communicate them. My teaching includes tutorials, marking, assessment support, and statistics across undergraduate and postgraduate settings.

## Units

### RMIT University

Undergraduate and postgraduate psychology units:

- BESC1433 Psychological Assessment and Individual Differences
- BESC1403 Personal Identity and Community
- BESC1437 Philosophy and Methodology of Psychology
- BESC1571 Counselling and Virtual Care
- BESC1514 Counselling and Professional Practices (Graduate Diploma)
- BESC1071 Psychology of Everyday Thinking
- BESC1512 Organisational and Motivational Psychology
- BESC1575 Thesis 1 (Honours thesis proposal)
- BESC1182 Developmental Psychology
- BESC1492 Field Placement (marking only)

### Cairnmillar Institute

- HON402 Research Methods
- HON401 Ethical Practice
- HON404 Evidence-based Practice and Practice-based Evidence
- HON405 Neuropsychology (marking only)

## Statistics and methods

I teach statistics conceptually before introducing software. Students use Jamovi and R to understand the question a method answers, inspect assumptions, interpret uncertainty, and report results clearly rather than treating an analysis as a sequence of clicks. My research methods experience includes systematic review, longitudinal modelling, measurement invariance, latent profile analysis, and machine learning.
